attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'right now', the either/or structure and the 'hundreds of dollars a user' figure. It drops the rhetorical tail about customers, which is fine. It is a firm present-tense observation, but a loose and partly rhetorical one.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no testable boundary. 'Experimental' revenue is undefined, and the claim gives no user cohort, duration or subsidy measure (provider cost vs API list price). Picking one of these would decide the result, so declining to score does not stretch the claim for or against the speaker.

evidence.note: A Tom's Hardware report from 2026-06-13, before the cutoff, citing SemiAnalysis. It values maximum subscription usage at API prices, which does not measure the provider's actual cost or subsidy per user. It is suggestive under one reading, but under the contract it cannot establish the claim.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm but vague observation. The claim defines no experimental-revenue boundary, user population, duration or subsidy measure, so neither support nor contradiction can be tested. The only evidence compares subscriptions with API list prices, which says nothing on provider losses, so it is context only. This is untestable as written, not a broken case.
